questions.q: What four capabilities does Driftwood's storefront platform now have, that it didn't at the start of this project?
options: A bigger marketing budget and a new logo
Containerization, Terraform-provisioned infrastructure, a CI/CD pipeline, and a correctly-scoped AWS backup target
A move away from Azure entirely to AWS
A complete rewrite of the application in a new programming language
questions.explain: The project added containerization, Terraform-managed infrastructure, CI/CD deployment, and a properly scoped cross-cloud AWS backup -- exactly what Priya and Casey originally asked for.

questions.q: How should the two mistakes found in this chapter be understood in the context of the overall project?
options: As a failure that undermines the project's success
As part of the success story — they were found, fixed, validated, and guarded against through the platform's own review discipline
As something that should have been hidden from stakeholders
As proof that Terraform and CI/CD don't actually help prevent mistakes
questions.explain: A platform's maturity is measured by how reliably real mistakes get found, fixed, validated, and guarded against -- not by pretending none occurred.

questions.q: What is the actual measure of this platform's maturity, according to the wrap-up?
options: Having zero mistakes ever occur
How reliably mistakes get found, fixed, validated, and turned into a guard against recurrence
How quickly the project was completed
How few people were involved in the project
questions.explain: The four-part pattern -- found, fixed, validated, guarded against -- not a zero-mistake record, is what the lesson identifies as the real measure of maturity.

questions.q: What has Casey Lindqvist signaled as the next phase for Driftwood's platform?
options: Shutting down the AWS backup entirely
Taking the platform to full Kubernetes and multi-cloud scale
Reverting back to a single, non-containerized deployment
Switching the entire platform to a different cloud provider exclusively
questions.explain: The next phase is full Kubernetes and multi-cloud scale -- named as a direction, with no further specifics given here.

questions.q: Why doesn't this wrap-up describe the specifics of the next phase?
options: Because there is no next phase planned
Because the next phase is a separate project with its own lessons and scenario, and this wrap-up's job is to close this project cleanly, not preview the next one
Because Casey Lindqvist has not yet decided whether to proceed
Because Kubernetes and multi-cloud topics are considered out of scope for Driftwood entirely
questions.explain: The next phase is deliberately left undescribed here since it belongs to a separate, future course with its own scenario.
